A M6.1 earthquake struck about **144 km southeast of Hasaki, Japan**, at 10:39 UTC on 6 November 2026, at a depth of about 29 km ([Defcon Level](https://www.defconlevel.com/alert/2026-11-06-usgs-earthquakes-m-6-1-156-km-se-of-hasaki-japan); [Earth Today](https://earthquaketoday.org/japan/hasaki-japan-M6.1-us7000twg9)). The coordinates given are about 34.97°N, 142.12°E, which is offshore east of Honshu.

I couldn't open the USGS event page directly, so these details come from secondary sites that cite USGS data. The Earth Today page also lists some distances and directions inconsistently (for example, it calls Tokyo "WNW" of the epicentre, which doesn't fit the coordinates). Check the USGS event page for the official details.

A separate M6.1 in the Fiji region occurred on 5 November (17:21 UTC), so it isn't the event you asked about.
